OCTOBER FIELD LOG — CAT HEAD AREA, LAKE MARION

This is a retrospective of our firsthand October fishing trips, not a claim that the same fish are holding there today. October's fishing gave us a documented starting point for evaluating the seasonal move into November.

OCTOBER 5 — Our trip produced approximately 240 pounds of catfish, including four fish over 50 pounds. Wind was reported around 7 mph from the north-northeast to north-northwest. These are trip totals, not a lakewide catch forecast.

OCTOBER 13 — Fishing near Cat Head, morning surface water temperature was about 75.7°F. Bait was observed in approximately 10–18 feet of water. The recorded catch included a 6-pound channel catfish and an 8-pound blue catfish, followed by a blue reported around 40 pounds later in the trip.

OCTOBER 21 — Near Cat Head, water temperature ranged from approximately 70.3°F to 72.8°F during the trip. We caught blue catfish weighing approximately 30 and 25 pounds in about 18 feet of water, and later a blue around 40 pounds in approximately 22 feet on an upslope.

WHAT THE LOG TELLS US — During the documented October outings, productive water included bait-related structure and depth changes in the upper-teen to low-20-foot range. The October 21 upslope catch shows why the relationship between contours can matter as much as any single depth. These results document where and how we fished on those dates; they do not establish a current bite at Cat Head or across Lake Marion.

NEXT STEP — November coverage will investigate a new location and compare its contours, bait, water conditions, sonar observations and actual fishing results against this October baseline. Public reports explain the general-area structure and reasoning; exact GPS positions and advanced tactics are available to Master Fisherman Patreon supporters.

DIVERSION CANAL FLOW ASSESSMENT — November 17, 2026 (11:19 a.m. EST)

STATUS: ACTUAL DIVERSION CANAL FLOW NOT INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED. Santee Cooper operational data updated November 17, 2026, reports daily lake elevations through November 16 (one-day reporting lag). Individual observation times and common gauge vertical datum have NOT been independently reconciled: USGS Elloree 02169921 and Pinopolis 02172000 pages returned HTTP 403. No direct canal current, velocity, or discharge measurement was verified.

OPERATOR DAILY ELEVATIONS (feet, not verified simultaneous/same-datum): November 16 Lake Marion 74.16, Lake Moultrie 74.09; nominal Marion-minus-Moultrie difference +0.07 ft. November 15 Marion 74.19, Moultrie 74.14; nominal difference +0.05 ft. Marion fell 0.03 ft; Moultrie fell 0.05 ft; nominal difference widened 0.02 ft. These are arithmetic differences of operator daily values, NOT verified instantaneous hydraulic head. November 17 elevations remain unavailable in this daily table.

OPERATIONS (operator feed updated November 17; tentative schedules, not observed generation): Jefferies Hydro November 17 6 a.m.–midnight; November 18 4 a.m.–10 p.m. St. Stephen not scheduled November 17 or 18. November 16 daily facility discharge table lists Jefferies 4,686 and St. Stephen 0 (units not independently verified here); these facility figures do NOT measure Diversion Canal discharge, and generation schedules do not prove canal current.

INTERPRETATION — CONDITIONAL INFERENCE ONLY: If lake elevations are on the same vertical datum and represent comparable observation times, a higher Marion elevation would be consistent with potential Marion-to-Moultrie water movement. The nominal +0.07 ft difference is small and does not establish actual direction or strength of canal current. Wind setup, operations and local conditions can affect water movement. No qualitative current-strength assessment is supported. ACTUAL CANAL DIRECTION AND STRENGTH NOT INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED.

level_analysis: Daily lake-level readings above are published with USGS station timestamps. Review each gauge's vertical datum before comparing Lake Marion and Lake Moultrie. Water movement and reservoir operations require separate verification; elevation alone cannot establish canal discharge.
wind_analysis: The hourly wind forecast above provides broad guidance, but wind exposure varies by fetch, shoreline orientation, gusts and travel route. Check the selected forecast area, recheck conditions before launching, and do not treat a forecast as a measured on-water reading.
temperature_analysis: WATER TEMPERATURE REPORT — November 17, 2026 (8:05 a.m. EST). CURRENT READINGS NOT VERIFIED. Attempts to retrieve the primary USGS water-temperature feeds for Lake Marion Pineville (02171000, bottom-water sensor) and Lake Moultrie Moncks Corner (02172002, downstream tailrace canal) did not return current November 17 observations or timestamps. Accordingly no November 17 temperatures, observation freshness, or verified 24-hour changes are reported. For historical context only, the ATSC dashboard screenshot from November 16 displayed Pineville bottom water 61.3°F and Moncks Corner tailrace water 62.8°F, both timestamped November 16 at 7:45 a.m. EST; those figures are NOT today's readings and were not independently confirmed with the USGS API. These sites measure different water environments, neither lake-wide surface temperature. Cooling can influence baitfish and blue catfish distributions, but these sensors cannot establish fish locations or feeding activity. Check the live dashboard timestamps before using readings: https://atsclakes.com/#conditions . Primary stations: https://waterdata.usgs.gov/monitoring-location/02171000/ and https://waterdata.usgs.gov/monitoring-location/02172002/ .
